text:
- chief complaint: the patient is a post-bilateral reduction mammoplasty patient presenting for routine postoperative follow-up, with concern about widened, bothersome scar on one breast.
- history of present illness: the patient had bilateral reduction mammoplasty on 10-10-2020. A lump under the left breast noted at a prior visit in March had resolved, and the patient has been performing massage. Back pain has resolved. The patient reports the scars are bothersome and has been using scar gel daily.
- physical examination: incisions well healed; no signs of infection or redness on either breast. Scars have widened slightly, and the doctor is not concerned. Photographs taken for monitoring.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: bothersome scar on one breast; previously noted left breast lump (now resolved); back pain (now resolved). No chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: mederma scar gel, applied twice daily to scars.
- follow-up instructions: return in six months to reassess scars; scar revision discussed but deferred until at least one year post-op; continue scar gel and massage twice daily.
